answer: No invoice counts until the buyer cosigns. Each client escrows collateral matching the sale; if the registry proves buyer and seller share an operator and a wallet, the whole ring's bonds are forfeited together. A farm invoicing its own wallets stakes its own fortune and loses it at once. Outside clients risk little; honest sellers never trigger clawback. Cosigning becomes a priced service: honest buyers charge a premium the farm must keep buying from strangers free to refuse. Trust hardens like timber; clones are one dune one wind flattens. An opal bought with borrowed money proves nothing.
